items.title: Report Identifies Path to Stronger State Flood Resilience and Insurance Protections
items.summary: A new report for California policymakers assesses current flood modeling practices and offers eight recommendations to improve how mitigation infrastructure is reflected in the catastrophe models that are used to set insurance prices.

items.title: What These Emmy-Nominated Shows Reveal About Hollywood’s Impact on Local Economies
items.summary: Ahead of this year’s Emmy Awards, UC San Diego professor of Ethnic Studies Curtis Marez discussed what four nominated shows—Widow’s Bay, Pluribus, DTF St. Louis and Beef—reveal about Hollywood’s effect on the places where television is made.

items.title: Wildfire Losses Have Lasting Economic Consequences for Homeowners
items.summary: A new National Bureau of Economic Research from the University of California San Diego shows that wildfire damage can have long-term economic consequences for households, resulting in income losses, relocation of residents as well as slow rebuilding for several years after a fire.

items.title: Are Tariffs Making Prices Go Up?
items.summary: As Americans continue to worry about the cost of living, U.S. tariffs are back in the news. So we asked international trade economist and School of Global Policy and Strategy Dean Caroline Freund the question on many consumers' minds.

items.title: Why a Doctor Saying ‘It’s Normal’ Can Backfire
items.summary: Research shows that patients often interpret normalizing language to mean treatment isn’t necessary, but the misunderstanding can be prevented.
